clue.text: Skins decapitated fish

indicators.note: to decapitate is to cut off the head, so the opening letter of the word goes

blocks.note: peels are the skins of fruit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Skins' reads as a verb applied to the fish, but it is a noun giving PEELS, which loses its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long, snakelike creatures that are true members of the fish family.

clue.text: King upset over old woman's abnormal dryness

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Rex is Latin for king, as in royal signatures
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
one's old woman is informally one's mother, or ma

explanation.surface: An elderly lady suffers some dry complaint after a king is overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like it places one piece above another, but here it supplies a letter of its own, from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Xeroma is a medical term for excessive dryness of the eye's conjunctiva, from Greek xeros, dry.

clue.text: Fan of 'dictator's' criminal traits a little simple

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or wrong, so these letters are bent out of order
only a small portion of the word is wanted, namely its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An admirer of a tyrant shows crooked, rather simple-minded traits.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks round 'dictator's' flag a loose sense: a tsar was an autocrat rather than strictly a dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarist is a supporter of the tsar, the absolute ruler of imperial Russia, and of autocratic rule generally.

clue.text: Comfortable with weapon

blocks.note: W is a standard abbreviation for with
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a link word, but it supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being warm and snug is a state of physical ease, as when someone is cosy indoors.

clue.text: Spot excited punter over the moon

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so these letters are jumbled
to be over something is to cover it, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: taken as written
Io is one of the moons of Jupiter

explanation.surface: A gambler's winning bet has left them thrilled and delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the moon' begs to be read as one idiom for delight; split it, and 'the moon' is a specific moon, Io. A punter is a gambler in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot on the skin is a small skin eruption, the medical word for a rash or pimple breaking out.

clue.text: English company head is keen environmentalist

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Co is the abbreviation for company
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: The boss of a British firm turns out to be a committed green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a company boss, but it is the slang word for the head itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An eco-nut is an informal, slightly mocking name for someone obsessively devoted to ecological causes.

clue.text: Most recent three points

blocks.note: north, east and west are three points of the compass
-est is the ending that makes an adjective mean 'most'

explanation.surface: A scorer tallies three points for the latest result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' does double duty: it is part of the definition and also stands for the superlative ending that follows three compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Newest is the superlative of new, describing whatever arrived latest of all.

clue.text: Follow one another and rob graveyards over time?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing sitting over another comes first, reading from the top

blocks.note: to take is to steal
T is the abbreviation for time
funeral urns are where ashes rest, a whimsical stand-in for burial places, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Grave robbers work in rotation, plundering cemeteries over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking urns would be robbing graves, so the surface comes close to the wordplay; the question mark admits that urns are only loosely graveyards.
explanation.definitionFit: To take turns is an idiom for doing something in rotation, each person going after the previous one.

clue.text: Plant paste jewellery item?

blocks.note: paste is imitation gemstone, so it is a sham
rock is slang for a gem, especially a diamond

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a plant could be made into a piece of costume jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paste' looks like a verb or glue, but it is the glass used in fake gems. A fake rock is literally a sham rock.
explanation.definitionFit: The shamrock is a small three-leaved clover, the botanical emblem of Ireland.

clue.text: See 17
Spike's cat outside looking miserable

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: mog, or moggy, is British slang for a cat
a pin is a small spike

explanation.surface: Spike's pet cat sits outdoors, looking glum.
explanation.walkthrough: Spike reads as the name of a person or dog owning the cat, but it is a plain noun; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Moping is sulking listlessly, which shows on someone's face as a dejected, unhappy expression.

clue.text: "Shut up!" Bill's back interrupting nitpicker

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so the letters are read right to left
to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: pent, as in pent-up, means shut up or confined
a bill is a poster, and AD is short for advertisement

explanation.surface: Someone tells a fussy critic to be quiet as Bill returns to cut in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up!' looks like an order to be silent, but it is an adjective meaning penned in. Bill is a poster, not a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant fusses over trivial points of detail, which is exactly what a nitpicker does.

clue.text: Letter and when it should get here

blocks.note: first meaning: the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet
second meaning: the abbreviation for estimated time of arrival

explanation.surface: Someone wonders when the post will deliver a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a posted letter and its arrival time; one meaning is an alphabet letter, the other an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is a Greek character, and ETA stands for estimated time of arrival, the expected moment something turns up.

clue.text: Woman is not with children

indicators.note: not being with something means going without it, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: issue is a formal word for offspring
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A woman is childless.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a statement about a woman's family; 'children' is the legal word issue, from which the word 'is' is taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: Sue is a common female first name, a short form of Susan.

clue.text: Self-admirer in prison after setback? A no, I'm sorry

indicators.note: a setback sends something backwards, so the letters run in the opposite direction
sorry means in a poor or wretched state, so the letters are in disarray
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a cage is a prison
the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A vain man jailed after a setback refuses to apologise: 'No, I'm sorry'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'm sorry' reads as an apology, but 'sorry' is the signal to rearrange the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An egomaniac is obsessively absorbed in themselves, a person whose chief admiration is reserved for their own person.

clue.text: Keen on horse that's not first

indicators.note: whatever is not first is missing its leading part, so the opening letter goes

blocks.note: a pinto is a piebald or spotted horse

explanation.surface: Someone fancies a horse that never finishes first.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests backing an also-ran in a race; 'not first' describes the word, not the horse's placing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something is an informal idiom for being enthusiastic about it, as in into jazz.

clue.text: Strokes oarsmen practised for upcoming sports competition

indicators.note: something practised has been worked over and drilled, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rowers rehearse their strokes ahead of a coming regatta.
explanation.walkthrough: The rowing picture points to a boat race, but the competition is played on a green baize table with cues.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masters is an annual invitation snooker tournament held in London each January, so it was a forthcoming sporting event.

clue.text: Unfit, fat Don out running from one place to another

indicators.note: something unfit is in poor shape, so these letters lose their order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
O suggests nought, as a batter who is out may be for a duck
R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: An overweight, unfit academic is out jogging back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: This parse is uncertain: the six letters of 'fat Don' supply most of the answer, and the remaining O and R seem to come from cricket shorthand. A don is a British university lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: To and fro is an idiom for moving back and forth repeatedly between two places.

clue.text: Twister split American party

blocks.note: torn means split apart
A is a standard abbreviation for American
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A slippery politician divides a US political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American party' suggests the Democrats or Republicans, but it is two separate pieces: a letter and a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Twister is an American informal name for a tornado, a violently spinning column of air.

clue.text: Judd's content to go up to green ultimately - or brown?

indicators.note: the content of something is what lies inside it, so only the inner letters are kept
in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top
ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: the inner letters of the name
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A colour choice for something of Judd's: should it be green, or brown?
explanation.walkthrough: The colour words in the surface set a trap: 'green' contributes one letter, and 'brown' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dun is a dull greyish-brown colour, often used for horses.

clue.text: Reveal relative caught short by tree

indicators.note: being caught short means coming up short, so the word is cut and loses its final letter

blocks.note: an uncle is a relative
an oak is a tree

explanation.surface: A relative caught short behind a tree risks exposing himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught short' is a British idiom for urgently needing a toilet away from home, which is why the relative is by a tree; here it means docked.
explanation.definitionFit: To uncloak is literally to take off a cloak, and figuratively to expose or make visible what was hidden.

clue.text: Pull and snap uncovered bone

indicators.note: uncovering something strips its outer layer, so the outside letters go and the inside stays

blocks.note: the inner letters of the word
the inner letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone tugs at a bone and breaks it open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' reads as an exposed bone, but it applies to both words before it, each losing its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two long bones of the forearm, on the little-finger side.

clue.text: Picked up writer's books

blocks.note: Edward Lear was the Victorian writer of nonsense verse
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone collected an author's volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' reads as collecting books, but it means acquired knowledge. NT is the usual crossword shorthand for the New Testament books.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a skill or language is to acquire it casually, so picked up is a synonym for learnt.

clue.text: Bad thing to celebrate endlessly

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its closing letter

blocks.note: to sing is to celebrate, as in singing someone's praises

explanation.surface: It is wrong to keep partying without end.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a moral warning against endless revelry; 'endlessly' applies to the word, not the partying.
explanation.definitionFit: A sin is a wicked act, a transgression against moral or religious law.

clue.text: Listen in to nurse

blocks.note: first meaning: pay attention, heed what is said
second meaning: look after a patient

explanation.walkthrough: 'Listen in to' suggests eavesdropping on a nurse; split after 'in', each side is a meaning of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both paying heed to what someone says and caring for someone, as a doctor attends patients.

clue.text: Concerning sign of urtica running riot

indicators.note: running riot means behaving wildly and out of control, so the letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; urtica is the botanical genus of nettles

explanation.surface: A worrying sign that nettles are spreading out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concerning' looks like 'worrying', but it means 'about', so the definition is an adjective describing a zodiac sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Tauric means relating to a bull, and so to Taurus, the bull among the zodiac signs.

clue.text: Republican with no real intelligence rebuffed left-wing attacker

indicators.note: a rebuff pushes something back, so the letters face the other way

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
artificial intelligence is not the real thing
red is a common label for a left-winger

explanation.surface: A dim-witted Republican is rejected by a left-wing assailant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No real intelligence' sounds like an insult to the Republican, but it defines artificial intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider is someone who makes a sudden assault, so it is a straightforward synonym for an attacker.

clue.text: Others in support for shot

blocks.note: first meaning: the remainder, everyone else
second meaning: the cue-supporting stick used in snooker or billiards

explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the snooker theme continues: in snooker a rest is a stick with a crossed head that supports the cue for awkward shots.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the remaining people or things and a prop on which a player lays the cue.

clue.text: Temptation to take sweetheart on one's holiday

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one piece goes inside another
one piece placed on another sits directly alongside it in reading order

blocks.note: a lure is a temptation or enticement
the heart of 'sweet' is its middle letter
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: It's tempting to take one's sweetheart away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' looks like a lover, but it splits into a word and the instruction to keep its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time away from work, which is what a holiday provides.

clue.text: Electric shavers are useless at first for hairy bloke

indicators.note: at first points to the opening, so only the initial letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: the initial letter of each word

explanation.surface: Electric razors are no good for a very hirsute man.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface joke is apt: a man that hairy would defeat any electric razor.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau was born covered in red hair, and his brother Jacob describes him as a hairy man.

clue.text: Silly arse is beginning to needle lady

indicators.note: silly means foolish and muddled, so these letters are mixed up
the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A foolish twit starts teasing a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly arse' is a British insult for a fool, but 'Silly' is only the signal to rearrange the letters that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerissa is Portia's lady-in-waiting in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, and a woman's name generally.

clue.text: Firm initially in short discussion about union

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is kept
something short is cut off, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
the first letter of the word
a talk is a discussion

explanation.surface: A company's opening move in brief negotiations about the trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union in the business surface, but here it is sexual union. 'Initially' applies only to the word 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coital is the adjective from coitus, sexual intercourse, so it means relating to bodily union.
